clusters.state_of_play: An Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 cargo plane (Flight 7598) arriving from Puerto Rico overran a diagonal runway at Miami International Airport shortly before 2 p.m. EDT Sunday, struck two vehicles — a cleaning-company van and an SUV — and caught fire; NTSB says all five people killed were occupants of the van, while five others were injured (three critically); the two-person crew survived. Victims have been identified as Cuban immigrants who had fled Cuba. New video shows a survivor crawling from the plane and a person found alive in a crushed car near the crash site. NTSB recovered the flight data and cockpit voice recorders; initial flight data shows signs consistent with the pilots attempting a go-around before the crash, and investigators are examining whether the plane touched down too far down the runway to stop safely; the aircraft came to rest about 1,300 feet past the runway end. NTSB is set to interview the surviving pilots. All runways closed; FAA and NTSB continue investigating.
